title: performance(canary): adaptive auto-detection for perf regressions and rollout guards
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Our perf canary currently relies on static thresholds for latency and throughput which require manual tuning per workload and lead to frequent false positives during bursty traffic. This PR implements an adaptive auto-detection algorithm plus rollout guards with hysteresis to reduce noisy aborts while preserving fast rollback for true regressions.

What this change does: 1) Adds an adaptive detector that computes baseline latency/throughput distributions per route and uses a configurable sensitivity window to flag regressions relative to a rolling baseline (configurable lookback and percentile targets). 2) Introduces a hysteresis-based rollout guard so brief spikes do not trigger immediate aborts; regressions must persist for N consecutive evaluation windows or exceed a high-confidence threshold to block a rollout. 3) Integrates KV-aware thresholds for stateful decoding workloads (short prefix vs long prefix behavior). 4) Exposes new config knobs in canary config (sensitivity, lookback_minutes, consecutive_windows, high_confidence_factor) with safe defaults. 5) Updates observability: dashboard panels (P50/P95/P99, request rate, dropped tokens), alert rules, and an audit log entry on canary-block events.

Why this approach: Adaptive detection reduces operational overhead and improves SLO alignment by learning workload shape instead of relying on global static cutoffs. Hysteresis prevents churn on noisy signals and makes rollouts more predictable. KV-aware thresholds avoid flagging stateful models that have different latency characteristics.

Testing: - Unit tests for detector statistics and hysteresis state machine (tests/perf/test_detector_unit.py). - End-to-end perf canary smoke test that runs against a synthetic trace generator (tests/perf/test_detector_end2end.py). - Canary simulation harness updated to replay historical traces with injected regressions; verified behavior on multiple routes.

Files changed (high level): see files_changed field for a concise list.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind canary.autodetect.enabled=false by default for immediate safety. After merge we will enable for internal staging for 48 hours, monitor P95, and then opt into incremental production routes. Metrics to watch: canary_block_rate, canary_false_positive_rate (estimated via manual labeling), downstream error rate.

Related: Linear ENG-4821 (adaptive perf detection), ENG-5210 (rollout guard hysteresis). Example canary config: https://linear.app/ENG/board/ENG-4821/sample-canary-config (internal link).

Checklist:
- [x] Detector algorithm implemented and unit tested
- [x] Hysteresis state machine implemented
- [x] Config knobs and documentation added (docs/perf_canary.md)
- [x] Observability panels & alerts updated
- [x] End-to-end smoke tests added
- [x] Feature gated for safe rollout
commits_summary: 6 commits: initial detector implementation; add hysteresis state machine; KV-aware threshold hooks; config schema + validation; tests and examples; docs and dashboard updates
discussion:
Marcus Patel (reviewer): Can we please call out how the lookback window interacts with autoscaling bursts? Suggest adding an upper cap to the lookback so a long quiet period doesn't over-smooth.

Ava Chen (author): Good point added a max_lookback_minutes config and updated detector to fall back to a minimum sample count before trusting the baseline. See commit 'config schema + validation'.

Sofia Rodriguez (reviewer): Tests look thorough. One comment: the audit log entry should include the computed effect size and the baseline percentiles for post-mortem.

Ava Chen: Added effect_size and baseline_percentiles to the audit log in 'hysteresis.py' and included the fields in the docs.

Ethan Liu (reviewer): CI flaky test (test_detector_end2end) failed on first run due to timing; we should increase timeouts in harness.

Ava Chen: Increased harness timeouts and reworked synthetic trace generator to avoid race conditions. CI rerun passed.

Marcus Patel: Approved after small nits. Sofia Rodriguez: Approved. Ethan Liu: Approved and requested final staging rollout to be coordinated with SRE.
release_notes: Adds adaptive perf canary detection with hysteresis-based rollout guards. Feature is gated off by default; enables automatic detection of persistent latency/throughput regressions, reduces false positives, and provides KV-aware thresholds for stateful decoding workloads. Includes new dashboard panels and alerts.
